acceptance_evidence: GitHub Actions checks on the implementation PR
CCA structured verdict recording ISS-05 and ISS-11 as pass
.shiki ledger entries for the tdd and code-review skill invocations
completion_conditions: The task schema defines a field that carries the AFK/HITL classification, and docs/agents/checklists.md ISS-05 names that field plus a total fallback derivation, so ISS-05 is judgeable from the record for every task including the 153 registered before the field existed.
Both task-registration paths in scripts/shiki_tasks.py emit the AFK/HITL field and carry the plan-declared cca_checklist_profile, so ISS-11 stops being unsatisfiable-by-construction.
A binder test in tests/test_paired_invariants.py fails when a blocking ISS row exists with no backing task-schema field, or when the two registration paths stop emitting that field.
non_goals: Backfilling dispatch_mode or cca_checklist_profile into the 153 existing .shiki/tasks records (cross-task mirror rewrite is blocked by contract immutability; it belongs to the already-registered migration-mode tasks).
Promoting any field to task.schema.json required or validate_shiki.TASK_REQUIRED.
Making the CCA deterministic about which checklist FAMILIES apply to a PR (the broader nondeterminism this defect exposed).
Adding a SADR (docs/adr numbering 0020 and 0021 are already claimed by other planned tasks).
outcome: Blocking checklist item ISS-05 (and ISS-11) can be satisfied deterministically from a registered Shiki task record, so the CCA verdict on a Contract-PR-registered task stops flipping between complete and refused on identical content.
title: Bind every blocking ISS checklist item to a field the task schema defines
